inspiration.observed_pattern: A PostgreSQL category search uses ILIKE to find a case-insensitive substring in a nullable description column.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Translated ILIKE into explicit LOWER(column) LIKE LOWER(pattern) expressions so the fixture does not depend on a database collation. The independently authored report also classifies NULL descriptions separately and retains them alongside matching categories; schema, rows, labels, and reporting purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Categories 11, 12, and 15 contain DISCUSS as a case-insensitive substring. Category 14 has a NULL description and is retained as missing, while category 13 is a non-matching description and is excluded. The result distinguishes matching text from NULL without relying on collation behavior.
determinism_notes: Category IDs are unique and fixed; the report is ordered by category ID and contains no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE catalog_categories (category_id INT PRIMARY KEY, category_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, description VARCHAR(160) NULL)

INSERT INTO catalog_categories VALUES (11, 'Compiler', 'Discuss release blockers before the next cut'), (12, 'Language', 'weekly discussion notes'), (13, 'Database', 'Index maintenance agenda'), (14, 'Support', NULL), (15, 'Research', 'DISCUSS experimental query planning')

steps.sql: SELECT category_id, category_name, CASE WHEN description IS NULL THEN 'missing' WHEN LOWER(description) LIKE LOWER('%DISCUSS%') THEN 'match' ELSE 'miss' END AS match_state FROM catalog_categories WHERE description IS NULL OR LOWER(description) LIKE LOWER('%DISCUSS%') ORDER BY category_id

checks.sql: SELECT category_id, category_name, description FROM catalog_categories ORDER BY category_id
